title: [replay r3] feat(desktop): float "Your video is ready" outside the app window
body:
> **Replay of [niway-dev/kaipu-record#466](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/466), run 3** for the code-review benchmark. Same base and head commits as the round-1 replay (a second branch name on the same commit, so the reviewer sees a fresh pull request). Never merged. Method: [wachiman/docs/benchmark](https://github.com/niway-dev/wachiman/tree/main/docs/benchmark).

---

## What

After a recording, "Your video is ready" (NIW2-584, #455) now **floats on the desktop** in its own window instead of sitting in the main window's status stack. The owner expected it to behave like a custom notification: visible even when Kaipu is hidden, minimized or behind another app.

It reuses the screenshot capture toast's pattern (`main/screenshots/capture-toast-window.ts`):

- **Window** (`main/recording/recording-ready-window.ts`): frameless, transparent, always on top (`floating`), a non-activating `panel` on macOS, shown with `showInactive` so it never takes focus from the app the user is in. `setContentProtection(true)` keeps it out of later recordings and screenshots. It joins every Space while shown, like the toast. It sits in the top-right corner of the display the take recorded (`RecordingHubHandle.lastTakeDisplayId()`), or the display under the pointer when that is unknown. The renderer reports the card's height so the window fits it.
- **Content**: the same `PostRecordingCard`, so the title, the "Master · full quality" tag, the duration · resolution · size line, the question, the YouTube / TikTok / GitHub chips, More places, Edit first, Open, × and the footer keep their styles and i18n. It is rendered from its own entry, `?window=recording-ready`.
- **Actions**: every action closes the window, then main shows and focuses the main window and sends it a typed hand-off (`recording-ready:open`). The renderer turns the hand-off into a route with the existing helpers: `preparePath` for chips and More places (so the Prepare → Export rename on the sibling branch follows), `editorPathFor` for Edit first, and the recording page for Open.
- **Lifetime**: no timer. × or Escape closes it. The next recording replaces it in the same window.
- **No duplicates**: the recording page still decides *when* the card shows (fresh recording, local video, Settings toggle on). It asks main once per arrival, after the file has been read, so the card opens with its numbers. Main answers `false` when it cannot create the window, or the IPC fails, and only then does the page show the in-app card.

Contract: `shared/types/recording-ready.ts` (payload, actions, hand-off, validation of everything that crosses IPC). It has no value imports, per the preload rule in CLAUDE.md.

## Why

The in-app card could not be seen at the moment it matters. When the user is back in another app after stopping a take, or the main window is hidden, the question "Where do you want to send it?" never reached them.

## Notes for review

- **Escape needs a click into the card first.** The window is `focusable: true` but never focuses itself. A window that never takes focus cannot receive key presses, and a global Escape shortcut would take Escape away from every other app.
- **The fallback covers only creation failures.** A window that is created but fails to load its renderer shows nothing. It does not fall back to the in-app card.
- **Two small changes to `PostRecordingCard`.** A new optional `onOpen` prop: in the floating window, Open goes to the recording page, while in-app it still only closes the card. It also has a matching `openFloatingHint` tooltip in English and Spanish.
- **Touched outside the status-card stack:** the recording page (`library-detail-page.tsx`), only to replace the card's render with the ask and fallback; and `recording-hub.ts`, which now remembers the take's display.

Tests: the window manager (create, replace, close, display choice, resize, validation, action → hand-off mapping, failure → `false`, quit), the card window component, the hand-off → path mapping, the contract parsers, the hub's display, and the recording page's floating, fallback and not-shown paths. `bun run verify` passes. Not run in Electron.

Backlog: `apps/documentation/src/content/docs/backlog/floating-ready-window.md`. There is no Linear ticket, because the workspace hit its issue limit.

## How to test it yourself

1. Check out `feature/floating-ready-window`, run `bun install`, then `bun run dev` for the desktop app.
2. Make sure Settings → Export quality has the post-recording card on.
3. Record a short take of your main display and stop it. A "Your video is ready" card should appear at the top-right of that display, **outside** the Kaipu window, with the duration, resolution and size. The app you were in should keep focus.
4. Click into another app, or minimize or hide Kaipu. The card stays on top.
5. Click **TikTok**. The card closes, Kaipu comes to the front, and Prepare opens with TikTok selected. Repeat with **More places** (Prepare, nothing selected), **Edit first** (the video editor) and **Open** (the recording's page).
6. Record again and press **×**. The card closes and Kaipu stays where it was. Record again, click the card body, then press **Escape**. It closes.
7. Record twice without closing the card. There is only ever one card, showing the latest take.
8. With an external display, record that display. The card opens in that display's corner.
9. Leave the card up and start a screenshot or another recording of that display. The card must not appear in the result.
10. Check the Kaipu window: the in-app "Your video is ready" card no longer shows in its top-right stack.
